title: Dart, Source Code, Textable
documentation:
## Source language
The programming language of a source-code file. Caps that operate on code (linters,
formatters, parsers) match on the language tag rather than on a specific file
extension. Language and file extension are correlated but not identical: a `.h`
file may be C, C++, Objective-C, or Objective-C++ depending on context.

Dart source code.

## Role
Semantic-role markers distinguish how a value is used in a flow from how it is
stored. A textual file might be `code` (source code), `log` (log records), or
`page` (a single document page). Role is attached during cap declaration to make
routing decisions explicit.

The value is source code. Caps that operate on code (formatters, linters, parsers,
LSP-style analysers) match on this tag rather than on a specific language.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.
